summary: Since round 3, bash termination also signals every process whose process-group ID equals the original shell PID, even after the shell has exited. Two temp bash tests now fail on a timeout, and the coverage gate fails on ten lines. The new group-ID match can also signal an unrelated process group after the shell's PID is reused. The change is not ready.

findings.body: `signalBashProcesses` now adds every process with `pgid === input.processGroupId`. `terminate()` always passes `processGroupId: running.pid`, even after the shell has exited and Node has reaped it (lines 137 and 147). Consider the scenario covered by the durable E2E: a setsid descendant keeps the stdout/stderr pipes open, the shell exits, and the run continues until timeout or Stop. If no process remains in the shell's original group, the kernel can reuse that PID. A new process with that PID becomes leader of a group with the same number. Other detached bash runs from this server are such leaders. On Stop or timeout the `ps` scan then matches the unrelated group, and the function sends SIGTERM and SIGKILL to both `-pid` and `pid`. This reintroduces the stale-ID hazard fixed under F2. Match by process group only while the group is known to be ours. For example, match only while the shell has not exited (`exitCode`/`signalCode` null). Alternatively, match only when the same scan finds a process carrying `HALO_BASH_RUN_ID=<runId>` in that group, or another proof that the group is still ours. Rely on the run-ID marker and the pipe destruction otherwise.

The temp run fails. 'kills an orphaned setsid child ignoring SIGTERM on timeout' (line 18) and 'kills an untagged same-group child after the shell exits on timeout' (line 106) set `timeoutMs: 5000` for the bash command. Vitest's default test timeout is also 5000 ms, so each test times out before `runBash` resolves (the log shows 'Test timed out in 5000ms'). Use a short command timeout, as before (for example 1500 ms), or pass a larger per-test timeout. The failed vitest run also seems to have dropped server coverage, so the Thread.ts and threadRouter.ts lines covered in round 3 now show as uncovered. Re-run so that both temp vitest files pass and the gate reports them as covered.
